title: Adaptive session materialized mart with hot/cold storage tiering
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Console SLA/dashboards are running slow for multi-tenant slices and cost/latency attribution queries. Current nearline tables are highly normalized and require expensive joins for tenant-level weekly reports and top-N route queries. We need a curated materialized mart that serves the most common console analytics workloads with predictable latency, supports hot/cold retention for large tenants, and simplifies downstream dashboard queries and scheduled reports.

Goal: Design and deliver an adaptive session-level materialized mart (session_mart) that: 1) pre-aggregates common dimensions (tenant, route, model_variant, SDK), 2) stores invocation-level metrics (token_count, cost_estimate, latency_ms) with precomputed quantiles per bucket, 3) supports hot/cold storage tiering (30d hot, 365d cold) and compaction, and 4) includes migration and backfill plan with verification dashboards.
background: Console teams currently run expensive joins across invocation, route_config, tenant_metadata, and feature flags to generate weekly usage and billing rollups. Large tenants with many routes cause scan-heavy queries and OOMs on BI workers. Existing materialized views are fragmented and lack coherent TTL policy. We want a single curated mart optimized for slicing by tenant and route variant, and for export to billing and cost-optimization pipelines.
design_decisions: Star-like denormalized layout: session_mart rows represent aggregated session windows (1h/1d) and include denormalized tenant and route metadata to avoid joins.
Adaptive partitioning: partition by tenant_id for large tenants, else by date_bucket for small tenants; use partition pruning-friendly keys.

Hot/cold tiering: hot partitions (last 30 days) live on fast compute-backed storage with low-latency materialized refresh; cold partitions (31-365 days) are compacted into append-only parquet tiles and moved to cheaper storage.
Precomputed approximations: use t-digest sketches or DDSketch for latency quantiles per partition to avoid heavy sorts at query time.
Compaction policy: hourly to daily downsampling for cold data with configurable retention and point-in-time rollback support.

Row-level schema: keep invocation-level metadata minimal (invocation_id, session_id, tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, tokens_in, tokens_out, cost_usd_est, latency_ms_p50_p95) and surface additional attributes as JSON string for edge cases.
Backfill strategy: incremental backfill by tenant priority and time window with checkpointing and checksum validation.
Observability: expose ingestion lag, partition sizes, query latency percentiles, and compaction job success as Console dashboards and alerting rules.
Compatibility: ensure mart keys align with billing and console route canonical ids to allow easy joins by external consumers.
Security: enforce tenant-namespace aware ACLs for direct table access and surface via Console read APIs only.
Migration: dual-write to new mart during rollout window; fall back to normalized pipeline on mismatch detection.
acceptance_criteria: session_mart is available with hourly and daily grain views and contains at least 95% of fields used by top-20 most frequent Console queries.
Typical tenant-level weekly queries (top-N routes by cost) execute within SLA: p95 < 5s for medium tenants and < 30s for largest tenants using hot partitions.
Cost attribution values match existing billing exports within 0.5% for sample tenants after backfill and reconciliation.
Hot/cold tiering demonstrably reduces storage cost for >90% of tenants compared to keeping all data hot for 365 days (measure in first month after rollout).
Backfill completes for priority tenants (list provided) and checksums validate row counts and aggregated sums against source normalized tables.
End-to-end dashboards (ingest lag, partition health, compaction metrics) are created and alert thresholds are configured.
PRs for ETL code, schema migrations, and docs are merged and reviewed by infra, data platform, and console PMs.
implementation_tasks: Create schema DDL for session_mart and supporting nightly compaction jobs (ENG/infra SQL repo PR).
Implement ETL transformation job in Spark/Beam with idempotent checkpoints and tenant-aware partitioning.
Integrate sketch-based quantile aggregation (t-digest) into transformation pipeline and expose quantile columns.
Add compaction job to downsample cold partitions and export parquet tiles to cheaper storage class.
Add ACLs and catalog entries; update data catalog with lineage links to source invocation tables.
Develop backfill orchestration job with tenant prioritization, parallelism controls, and integrity checks.
Produce verification notebook and set of test queries for QA and owner sign-off.
Build monitoring dashboards and alerts in Console (ingest lag, partition growth, compaction failures, query SLA violations).
Run gradual rollout: dual-write for 2 weeks, compare outputs, then switch consumers to mart views.
Document migration runbook and rollback plan in Confluence and link from Console internal docs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Backfill may overload cluster and affect production; Mitigation: throttled concurrent backfills, dedicate backfill capacity window, and use snapshot reads.
Risk: Quantile approximation divergence; Mitigation: calibrate sketch error bounds, store raw sample buckets for validation, and provide fallback exact aggregations for small partitions.
Risk: Tenant-specific skew causing huge partitions; Mitigation: adaptive partitioning by tenant size and enforce per-partition size alerts and automatic sharding for oversized tenants.
Risk: Query compatibility issues for downstream consumers; Mitigation: keep compatibility views for normalized schema and provide mapping docs and example queries.
Risk: Unexpected cost if hot tier grows; Mitigation: daily cost projection alerts and auto-eviction policy for stale partitions.
migration_plan: Phase 0: Design review with Console PMs, Billing, and Data Platform (complete).
Phase 1: Implement DDL and ETL skeleton; run dry-run on dev cluster (2 weeks).
Phase 2: Backfill priority tenants and validate aggregates (3 weeks).
Phase 3: Dual-write in prod for 2 weeks, run automated checks and reconcile differences (2 weeks).
Phase 4: Flip consumers to mart views, monitor for issues, and deprecate old views after 30 days of stability.
